subject.title: Multi-agent orchestration is unstable: concurrent agents add/config overwrites, session-lock failures, and detached child work

question: Should #43367 remain the canonical umbrella while focused lock/delivery/fallback repairs land, or should maintainers replace it with narrower canonical issues after preserving the production evidence?
rationale: Current main fixes only slices of the reported behavior, and the remaining work crosses reliability bugs plus product choices around subagent completion, session ownership, detached child work, and heavy orchestration boundaries.

options.title: Keep umbrella, land focused repairs
options.body: Keep #43367 open as the umbrella while #86540/#86538/#44925/#92433/#89927-style focused fixes and proofs resolve concrete slices.

options.title: Promote narrower canonicals
options.body: Move remaining lock/delivery ownership to narrower issues such as #86538 and #44925 after linking this issue's production evidence there.

options.title: Defer broad orchestration design
options.body: Reject token-ring or hierarchy-framework scope for now and only keep narrow stability bugs active under existing agent/session architecture.

recommendation.title: Keep umbrella, land focused repairs
recommendation.body: Keep #43367 open as the umbrella while #86540/#86538/#44925/#92433/#89927-style focused fixes and proofs resolve concrete slices.

likelyOwner.reason: History shows broad recent ownership across subagent delivery, session locks, and product-level recovery/audit surfaces.
